sentences.text: Archaeodontosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic.
This animal is considered a probable sauropod possessing teeth similar to those of prosauropods.
The creature is known solely from a fossilized jaw containing many teeth with unusual characteristics.
It was likely a large quadruped with a long neck, tail, and columnar legs.
Estimates suggest it measured between 11 and 13 meters in length and weighed approximately 4 to 5 tonnes.
The typical sauropod evolutionary trend of having primitive jaws but developed teeth was reversed in this species.
Eric Buffetaut discovered the remains in 2005 in the Majunga Formation of Isalo III, Madagascar.
The type species Archaeodontosaurus descouensi was formally described in September 2005.
The genus name means "ancient-toothed lizard" and the specific name honors the collector Didier Descouens.
Archaeodontosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropoda.
It serves as an indicator of sauropod diversity in the Middle Jurassic of Madagascar.
The dinosaur lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Madagascar.
More precise dating places its existence between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bathonian age.
Archaeodontosaurus has posed significant problems for paleontologists regarding sauropod evolution.
Fossil evidence suggests there were at least two different sauropods in the Middle Jurassic of Madagascar.
